sec: Metabolic acidosis, the anion gap and NAGMA/HAGMA · p820

items.q: Match the causes of metabolic acidosis — 1) Acid generation  2) Exogenous acid  3) Endogenous acid  4) Alkali loss … A) GI and renal loss  B) Methanol  C) Ketoacids  D) Parent category
items.exp: Metabolic acidosis arises from acid generation (exogenous, e.g. methanol; endogenous, e.g. ketoacids) and from alkali loss (GI and renal). (Book p820)

items.q: Fill up: The printed example of an exogenous acid causing metabolic acidosis is ______.
items.exp: Acid generation is split into exogenous acid (methanol) and endogenous acid (ketoacids). (Book p820)

items.q: Which of the following is given as the endogenous acid example?
items.exp: Endogenous acid: ketoacids; exogenous acid: methanol. (Book p820)

items.q: Match the steps of the anion gap derivation — 1) Total cation vs total anion  2) Adding unmeasured species  3) Measured cation − measured anions … A) = unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation  B) Are equal  C) measured cation + unmeasured cation = measured anion + unmeasured anion
items.exp: Total cation = total anion; measured cation + unmeasured cation = measured anion + unmeasured anion; hence measured cation − measured anions = unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation. (Book p820)

items.q: The anion gap is defined as which difference, and equals which formula?
opts: Unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation; = Na⁺ − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻)
Unmeasured cation − unmeasured anion; = Na⁺ − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻)
Measured anion − measured cation; = (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻) − Na⁺
Unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation; = (Na⁺ + K⁺) − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻)
items.exp: Anion gap = unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation = Na⁺ − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻). (Book p820)

items.q: Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis (NAGMA) is also called:
opts: Hyperchloremic acidosis, because HCO₃⁻ is compensated by Cl⁻
Hypernatremic acidosis, because Na⁺ rises to replace H⁺
Lactic acidosis, because lactate replaces HCO₃⁻
items.exp: In NAGMA, HCO₃⁻ is compensated by Cl⁻, hence the alternative name hyperchloremic acidosis. (Book p820)

items.q: Match the NAGMA causes shown in the flowchart — 1) GI loss  2) GI example  3) Renal loss … A) RTA  B) VIPoma  C) Ureterosigmoidostomy
items.exp: NAGMA causes: GI loss (VIPoma and ureterosigmoidostomy) and renal loss (RTA). (Book p820)

items.q: A patient with a VIPoma and chronic watery diarrhoea has a normal anion gap acidosis. This fits which printed category?
opts: NAGMA from GI loss of alkali
NAGMA from renal loss of alkali
items.exp: VIPoma is printed under NAGMA – GI loss, whereas RTA is the renal loss cause. (Book p820)

items.q: High anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA) is characterised by:
items.exp: HAGMA: ↑ in unmeasured anions — the unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation difference widens. (Book p820)

items.q: Fill up: The mnemonic given for the causes of high anion gap metabolic acidosis is ______.
items.exp: HAGMA causes are remembered by KUSMAL — ketoacidosis, uremia, salicylates/paraldehyde, methanol, ethylene glycol (alcohol) and lactic acidosis. (Book p820)

items.q: Match the KUSMAL letters to their causes — 1) K  2) U  3) S  4) L … A) Lactic acidosis  B) Ketoacidosis  C) Salicylates/Paraldehyde  D) Uremia
items.exp: KUSMAL: K = ketoacidosis, U = uremia, S = salicylates/paraldehyde, M = methanol, A = ethylene glycol (alcohol), L = lactic acidosis. (Book p820)

items.q: Under ‘K’ of the KUSMAL mnemonic, the three printed ketoacidosis subtypes are:
A patient swallows antifreeze and develops a metabolic acidosis with a raised anion gap and an osmolal gap. Which KUSMAL entry explains it?
items.exp: Antifreeze (ethylene glycol) is printed as ‘Ethylene glycol (Alcohol)’ under KUSMAL and produces HAGMA. (Book p820)

items.q: All but one of the following belong to the KUSMAL list of HAGMA causes. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: KUSMAL lists ketoacidosis, uremia, salicylates/paraldehyde, methanol, ethylene glycol and lactic acidosis — paracetamol is not part of it. (Book p820)
